findings.text: §23 says "A sweep derives through that call, so a sweep gets the same bound", but a sweep resolves each run's reviewed head a second time outside the derivation: `sweep` calls `payload_for` per session (`obligation_snapshot.py:1025`), and `payload_for` calls `obligations._review_duty_item` for every review-classified row (`obligation_snapshot.py:~900`), which calls `recovery._review_head_and_tree` (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:367`) and so `_reviewed_run_head` — a reader the same section explicitly keeps at current behaviour ("Readers outside a derivation keep their current behaviour"). The sweep's total per-run resolution is therefore the derivation's count plus the slice's, so the sweep is not bounded by §23, while §24's harness times `fleet_state` alone and would not see the slice's share
